leftEvidence.title: The gathered believers pray David’s words about rulers

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Released apostles report threats; the community names God as creator, says the Holy Spirit spoke through David in Psalm 2, identifies gathered rulers around Jesus, and asks for bold speech.
points.right: Paul recounts Israel from Egypt through judges and Saul, says God raised David and testified about his heart and will, then announces Jesus from David’s offspring.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places Davidic psalm language becomes a prayer frame for present opposition inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places David’s character testimony and descendant promise form a hinge toward Jesus inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: Acts 4:23–31 and Acts 13:16–23 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Gospel and Apostolic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Paul moves from David’s selection to a Savior from his offspring

payload.tension: Acts 4:23–31 foregrounds Davidic psalm language becomes a prayer frame for present opposition; Acts 13:16–23 foregrounds David’s character testimony and descendant promise form a hinge toward Jesus. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
payload.title: The gathered believers pray David’s words about rulers / Paul moves from David’s selection to a Savior from his offspring
